headline: Advance Entry and Trail Permits for Southern Utah
reservation: Access to high-demand areas like Coyote Buttes North requires a lottery-based permit system months in advance. While local Kanab trails are generally open, nearby National Parks like Zion may require specific reservations for shuttles or iconic hikes. Always verify the latest system requirements on official government websites as procedures for entry and parking are subject to change.

days.title: Canyons and Animal Conservation

stops.name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
stops.detail: Visit this renowned sanctuary in Angel Canyon by booking a guided tour in advance to see their conservation efforts.

stops.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
stops.detail: Walk the shifting landscapes of these unique dunes, ideally in the early morning to avoid peak heat.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total driving; conditions vary on sand-access roads
days.note: Sand temperatures rise quickly; morning visits are recommended for walking.

days.title: High Desert Overlooks

stops.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
stops.detail: Drive north to view the amphitheaters of hoodoos from established rim overlooks like Sunset Point.

stops.name: Red Canyon
stops.detail: Stop at the visitor center along Scenic Byway 12 to see the distinctive red rock formations and arches.

days.driving: Allow 3.5 hours round-trip; high elevation can impact vehicle performance
days.note: Bryce Canyon is significantly higher and colder than Kanab; check for ice into late spring.

days.title: East Zion Exploration

stops.name: Zion-Mount Carmel Highway
stops.detail: Experience the historic tunnel and towering sandstone cliffs of Zion's quieter eastern entrance.

stops.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
stops.detail: A short, established walk providing views of the main Zion Canyon without needing the shuttle system.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours round-trip; check for oversized vehicle tunnel restrictions
days.note: Parking at the East Side trailheads is extremely limited and fills early.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Canyon Overlook and popular Kanab trailheads are small and often reach capacity early in the morning. Have a secondary local walk identified in case your first choice is full.

intel.title: Offline Navigation
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable or absent once you leave the Highway 89 corridor. Download regional maps and permit confirmations before departing Kanab for the day.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Fill your tank in Kanab before heading toward the North Rim or the Paria Plateau. Services are sparse on the long stretches between major gateway towns.

intel.title: Time Zone Awareness
intel.text: Utah follows Daylight Saving Time while nearby Arizona does not. Confirm if your tour operator or destination follows Mountain Daylight Time to avoid missing appointments.

intel.title: Unpaved Road Safety
intel.text: Routes like House Rock Valley Road are dirt-based and can become impassable for all vehicles after rain. Check the Bureau of Land Management office in Kanab for current road grades.

plan.arrival: Arrive via St. George or Page; collect supplies at local grocers in Kanab before checking into your desert lodging.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended for exploring unpaved backroads; check rental contracts for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at the Coral Pink Sand Dunes provides dramatic shadows, though cloud cover varies seasonally.
